concepts.name: Constitutional Framework of Tax Distribution: Articles 268–293
key_dimensions: Structural architecture — Union List, State List, Concurrent List taxation heads
Distinction between 'levy', 'collection', and 'appropriation' of taxes across Articles 268–272
UPSC trap: which taxes are levied by Union but collected/appropriated by States vs. shared vs. solely Union
Post-101st Amendment changes and how GST reshaped this framework

concepts.name: Article 268: Duties Levied by Union but Collected and Appropriated by States
key_dimensions: Current scope — stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques, promissory notes etc.
UPSC trap: these are NOT shareable taxes; States keep 100% of collections within their territory
Distinction from Article 269 taxes which are assigned to States
Historical inclusion of medicinal preparations (removed post-GST) as a trap item

concepts.name: Article 268-A (Repealed): Service Tax — Historical and Post-GST Significance
key_dimensions: Inserted by 88th Constitutional Amendment 2003; operationalized service tax sharing
Repealed by 101st Constitutional Amendment 2016 upon GST introduction
UPSC trap: candidates confuse this with Article 269-A which deals with GST on inter-State trade
Lesson on constitutional evolution — how a new article can be inserted and later repealed

concepts.name: Article 269: Taxes Levied and Collected by Union but Assigned to States
key_dimensions: Covers taxes on sale/purchase of goods (other than newspapers) in inter-State trade — now subsumed in GST
Distinction: 'assigned' means States receive 100% — not a sharing arrangement like Article 280
UPSC trap: Article 269 vs. Article 269-A — different mechanisms for different transactions
Net proceeds concept: what qualifies as 'net proceeds' for assignment purposes

concepts.name: Article 269-A: GST on Inter-State Supply — Levy, Collection, and Apportionment
key_dimensions: Inserted by 101st Amendment: IGST levied and collected by Union, apportioned between Union and States
Parliament prescribes the apportionment formula — GST Council recommends
UPSC trap: IGST revenue is NOT covered by Finance Commission; it is apportioned by a separate mechanism
Import transactions treated as inter-State supply — Union keeps customs but IGST on imports is shared

concepts.name: Article 270: Taxes Levied and Distributed Between Union and States (Divisible Pool)
key_dimensions: Core sharing mechanism — all taxes in Union List (except those in Articles 268, 269, 269-A, surcharges, cesses) form the divisible pool
Post-101st Amendment: CGST and additional excise duties on GST goods now brought under Article 270
UPSC trap: surcharges and cesses are explicitly excluded from divisible pool under Article 271
Finance Commission determines the vertical share (Union vs. States) and horizontal share (among States)

concepts.name: Article 271: Surcharges and Cesses — Exclusion from Divisible Pool
key_dimensions: Parliament can impose surcharge on any tax in Union List; proceeds go solely to Union
UPSC trap: Cesses (e.g., Health and Education Cess, Swachh Bharat Cess) are also excluded — a major fiscal federalism controversy
Growing share of cesses/surcharges in Union's gross tax revenue as a contemporary concern
15th Finance Commission highlighted this issue; connects to fiscal federalism debates

concepts.name: Finance Commission: Constitutional Basis and Mandate (Article 280)
key_dimensions: Constituted every 5 years by President; quasi-judicial body under Article 280
Mandate: recommend vertical devolution (Union–States split) and horizontal distribution (among States)
UPSC trap: Finance Commission also recommends grants-in-aid under Article 275, not just tax sharing
Distinction from Planning Commission/NITI Aayog — constitutional vs. extra-constitutional body

concepts.name: Vertical Devolution: Evolution Across Finance Commissions (1st to 15th)
key_dimensions: Progressive increase: 1st FC ~30% → 14th FC 42% → 15th FC 41% to States from divisible pool
14th FC's jump to 42% was landmark; 15th FC marginally reduced to 41% citing centrally sponsored schemes
UPSC trap: the 42%/41% figure applies to the divisible pool ONLY — not gross tax revenue of Union
Rationale factors: expenditure needs of States, own tax capacity, fiscal discipline

concepts.name: Horizontal Distribution Criteria: Equity vs. Efficiency Parameters
key_dimensions: 15th FC criteria: Income Distance (45%), Demographic Performance (12.5%), Forest & Ecology (10%), Tax Effort (2.5%), Area (15%), Population 2011 (15%)
UPSC trap: 15th FC used 2011 census population — southern States objected; 'demographic performance' added as compensation
Shift from income distance (equalisation) to rewarding efficiency — federal tension between equity and incentive
Comparison with 14th FC criteria to understand evolution

concepts.name: Article 275: Grants-in-Aid to States — Statutory Grants vs. Discretionary Grants
key_dimensions: Parliament may provide grants to States in need of assistance — on Finance Commission recommendation
Distinction: Article 275 grants are statutory (Finance Commission–recommended) vs. Article 282 discretionary grants
UPSC trap: Article 275(1) has a specific proviso for Scheduled Tribes welfare and raising administration standards in tribal areas
These grants are charged to Consolidated Fund of India — not subject to annual vote

concepts.name: Article 282: Discretionary Grants — Union and State Contributions for Public Purpose
key_dimensions: Both Union AND States can make grants for any public purpose, even outside their legislative competence
Historically used by Union to fund Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) — source of 'cooperative federalism' debate
UPSC trap: Article 282 grants are discretionary and votable — NOT charged to Consolidated Fund, unlike Article 275
States argue this creates dependency and distorts State priorities — fiscal federalism tension

concepts.name: GST Council: Constitutional Status, Composition, and Voting Mechanism (Article 279-A)
key_dimensions: Inserted by 101st Amendment — first time a constitutional body given joint tax policy-making role
Composition: Union Finance Minister (Chair) + State Finance Ministers; Union has 1/3 votes, States together have 2/3
UPSC trap: decisions require 3/4 majority of votes cast — NOT simple majority; Union veto effectively exists
Supreme Court in Mohit Minerals (2022): GST Council recommendations are not binding on Parliament/State legislatures — only persuasive

concepts.name: Consolidated Fund vs. Contingency Fund vs. Public Account: Tax Revenue Flow
key_dimensions: All tax revenues (Union's share) credited to Consolidated Fund of India (Article 266)
UPSC trap: 'charged' expenditures on Consolidated Fund (e.g., Finance Commission grants, debt servicing) vs. 'voted' expenditures
States' share of divisible pool transferred to respective State Consolidated Funds
Contingency Fund (Article 267) — imprest account, Parliament/Legislature can recoup; NOT a tax-sharing mechanism

concepts.name: Net Proceeds Concept: Calculation and Significance in Tax Sharing
key_dimensions: Net proceeds = gross tax collection minus cost of collection (Article 279 defines this)
Only 'net proceeds' of shareable taxes go into the divisible pool — UPSC frequently tests this nuance
Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) certifies net proceeds — adds audit accountability
UPSC trap: if cost of collection is high (e.g., small taxes), States may effectively get less than expected share

concepts.name: Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS): Fiscal Federalism Concerns
key_dimensions: Funded under Article 282 — Union directs spending in State subjects (Education, Health, Agriculture)
Rationalization exercises: 2015 (from 66 to 28 umbrella schemes); yet States claim conditionalities remain
UPSC trap: CSS spending bypasses Finance Commission framework — States must contribute matching funds creating fiscal pressure
14th FC recommended reducing CSS and increasing tax devolution — tension between two approaches

concepts.name: GST Compensation to States: Constitutional Guarantee and Its Expiry
key_dimensions: GST (Compensation to States) Act 2017: guaranteed 14% annual growth in revenue for 5 years (till June 2022)
Compensation funded by GST Compensation Cess on luxury/demerit goods — separate from divisible pool
UPSC trap: Compensation Cess was extended beyond 2022 to repay loans taken during COVID — NOT for direct State compensation
Post-2022 debate on States' revenue autonomy loss due to subsuming of VAT, entry tax, octroi into GST

concepts.name: Tax Devolution vs. Grants: Untied vs. Tied Funds Debate
key_dimensions: Tax devolution (Articles 270, 269) is untied — States spend as per their priorities (stronger fiscal autonomy)
Grants (Articles 275, 282) often come with conditions — weaker fiscal autonomy for States
UPSC trap: 14th FC consciously raised devolution and reduced grants to enhance State autonomy — a policy choice
Sector-specific grants (revenue deficit grants, disaster management grants, local body grants) under 15th FC

concepts.name: Inter-State Tax Disputes and Adjudication: Articles 286, 304, and Entry Tax Controversy
key_dimensions: Article 286 restricts States from taxing inter-State sales/purchases — prevents trade barriers
Article 304 allows States to impose taxes on imported goods equal to similar local taxes (non-discriminatory)
Entry Tax controversy: States levied entry tax on goods from other States — SC in Jindal Stainless (2016) upheld compensatory theory test
UPSC trap: after GST, entry tax subsumed — but pre-GST arrears and disputes still relevant for exam context

concepts.name: 15th Finance Commission: Key Recommendations and Controversies
key_dimensions: 41% vertical devolution (vs. 14th FC's 42%) — reduction linked to creation of J&K UTs and centrally funded obligations
Performance-based grants introduced: local bodies, health, education, agriculture — incentivizing outcomes
UPSC trap: 15th FC gave TWO reports — one for 2020-21 (transition year) and main for 2021-26 — different devolution ratios
National Disaster Risk Management Fund and State Disaster Risk Management Fund recommendations — fiscal federalism in disaster financing
